256	**LS-21 — Serialization, hash, summary, interchange.** *Persisted (canonical):* `schema_version`, `next_node_id`, `next_edge_id`, `next_seam_id`, `next_section_id`, `last_step_no` and the per-hook cursors `last_step_power`, `last_step_atmo`, `last_step_failure` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; the `def_table` CSR pair (`def_off`, `def_utf8`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; nodes and edges with every field of LS-3/LS-5 including tombstones; SeamRecords; sections with `dormant`, `dormant_since_step` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*, `rate_pm`, `stress_pm`, `stress_until_step`, `vented_mgu`, `radiated_dj`, `spilled_cool_ml`, `produced_mgu`, `breathed_mgu`, `produced_dj`, `burned_uml`, `spilled_heat_mdj` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, `discarded_*`, `withdrawn_*` (M16, per medium) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from web-map-and-transit)*; compartments `layout_room_ref`, `n_o2`, `n_inert`, `T`, `t_rem`, `fuel_puddle_ml` and the hysteresis memory `band_o2`, `band_p`, `band_t`, `p_prev` (the previous run's `P`), and the warn trackers `warn_since_o2`, `warn_since_p`, `warn_since_t` (i32 each) and `warn_bits` (u8) — canonical order after `p_prev` (+13 bytes per compartment, 65 for the MVP five) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*; every stored OPENING's `strain_gas` and `strain_heat` live bits (SEAL_STRAIN hysteresis, D.14); **and the three input queues** — `pending_draw` (compartment, crew, mGU), `pending_load` (node, `req_w`) and `pending_trace` (kind, subject, magnitude), each in arrival order and bounded (draw ≤ `MAX_CREW` × compartments, load ≤ 64, trace ≤ `MAX_FOOTPRINTS_PER_STEP`), plus the last applied `draw_grant` table. A snapshot can be taken on any tick, so a queue that held a breath, a trace or a load change between two hook ticks would otherwise be lost on restore and the restored run would diverge from the uninterrupted one *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. *Derived, never in a snapshot:* `V`, `exposed_tiles` (from Layout), components, trees, `path_cap`, degrees, id → slot maps, `served_pm`, descriptors, `P`/`p_o2`/`o2_pm`, last-emitted buckets, the cached hash. Rule: anything the next step depends on that is not re-derivable from persisted fields is persisted (`t_rem`, `tc_rem`, `fuel_rem`, `out_w`, `forced_mode_next`, `warn_since_step` with its `has_warn` bit, `thaw_until_step` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, the GA-T fields `mode_since_step`, `mode_key` and `isolated_at_step`, `dormant_since_step` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*, the three `pending_*` queues, the band and SEAL_STRAIN memory, the compartment warn trackers `warn_since_o2/p/t` and `warn_bits` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*); `served_pm` is not, because phase 2 recomputes it before use. `canonical_bytes()` = the persisted fields in a fixed documented order, each as `[u32 tag][u32 length][field.to_byte_array()]`, raw slot arrays with tombstones — native memcpy, no interpreted loop. **`block_hash()`** is published: cached, recomputed only when the block was written since the last hash, H64 over `canonical_bytes()` (H64 = the first 8 bytes of the SHA-256 that native `HashingContext` returns, read as a little-endian u64 — a truncated hash, never a hand-rolled 64-bit mix) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; the kernel's `state_hash` is registered as `state_hash(scope, T) = H64( T || world_seed || concat over b in scope sorted by block_id of (len(block_id) || block_id || schema_version || len(canonical_bytes(b)) || block_hash(b)) )` with `block_hash(b) = H64(canonical_bytes(b))` cached per block and invalidated by the dirty bit, and the Graph's `canonical_bytes()` and `block_hash()` feed it unchanged *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass after design review)*. The one-level Merkle form (`state_hash` over per-block cached hashes, H64 via native `HashingContext` or S0-d's winner) is **kernel amendment K-1, routed to the kernel owner as an ADR candidate** and not a rule of this GDD (R5). **SHARED_SUMMARY** (VS-B): per compartment `T_dC` (int16, 0.1 °C), `P` (u16), `p_o2` (u16), three bands (3 bits each); per node/edge `state` (3 bits) + `sev` (3 bits) + `served_q` (0..15); per loop component `pool_q`; active descriptors compact `(id, mode, sev, alarm_eligible, intensity bucket = intensity_pm / 100, since_steps, mode_steps, grow_steps, each saturating at 2^24 − 1)` — 7 bytes for the first six fields plus 3 bytes for each of the two GA-T ages, 13 bytes each, from which a client derives `fail_since_step` and the trail's own age so two MIRROR crewmates see equal trail extent, dullness and density (CR-10, VS-B) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from failure-and-trail-system; GA-T fields added 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*; seam list; about 0.4 KB at MVP, deltas ride the dirty keys; clients never receive `t_rem`, queues or RNG inputs — they receive truth, quantised. **Interchange (S-1, routed to Save/Load):** every Graph value stays below 2^53; the canonical form is packed int arrays; any JSON text form must carry the raw canonical bytes as base64 (`Marshalls.raw_to_base64`); `var_to_bytes` is not used — the `allow_objects` argument of the first draft is Godot 3-era and does not exist in 4.x, and Variant framing would put engine-version headers inside the hashed form *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; never a `Resource` for saves (R6; Godot JSON parses numbers as float — TD, sourced). Restore is two-phase (decode and validate into a scratch state, then swap); `restore(data, stored_version)` supports exactly version 1 in MVP, any other version is a reported failure, and every failure is a named `GRAPH_RESTORE_*` reason with the live state untouched (Section E). Type ids are append-only forever — the only forward-compatibility promise v1 makes.

258	**LS-22 — Falsifiability: perception-agnostic by construction.** No mutator argument carries a believed state; every argument is an id or a physical magnitude; the Graph never reads `PERCEPTION_OUT` (kernel CR-12) and `read_view` returns true values only, so a hallucinated "fixed" pipe (the Filter shows OK while `hp` = 2000) cannot change a Graph value and a hallucinated repair performs the real `repair_step` increments against the true `hp` — it costs time, not truth. Every gauge quantity has **one physical witness driven by the same Graph value**, so a lying instrument can be falsified by the world:
259	
260	| Gauge quantity | Physical witness (same value) | Channel (LS-14) *(Amended 2026-10-26 — CD-GDD-ALIGN)* |
261	|---|---|---|
262	| O2 pressure / fraction | `ATMO_THIN` band: breath audio and Suit's walk-only state (SE-27; no vignette) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from suit-and-equipment, sanity-and-hallucination-rules, perception-filter)*; scrubber hum via `served_pm` | consequence (Suit body cues, HUM_DROP at the scrubber) |
263	| Temperature | `ATMO_COLD`/`ATMO_HOT`: frost, breath fog, shiver, shimmer | consequence (trail VFX, Suit body cues) |
264	| Pressure | `AIRFLOW` draught and dust at openings, pull toward the hole *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from suit-and-equipment)* | consequence (draught, Suit body cues) |
265	| Pressure across a closed hatch | `SEAL_STRAIN` (D.14): CREAK at the rim, bowed hatch, rim frost when `|ΔT|` > `HATCH_DT_FROST_MC`; the `AIRFLOW` draught the moment it opens | consequence (acoustic class at the anchor, trail VFX) |
266	| Power | lamp brightness `served_pm`, hum pitch, relay clunk on STARVE | consequence (lamp brightness, HUM_DROP, CLANK); the breaker panel's own lamp is module-body |
267	| Coolant | pipe frost and drip descriptors, radiator glow, pump cavitation TICK | consequence (DRIP, frost trail, TICK); the radiator's glow sprite is module-body |
268	| Hull | hiss, debris stream, frost along the hole, groan TICK with `since_steps` | consequence (HISS, WIND, trail VFX, TICK) |
269	| Fuel | sight-glass is Instruments; the puddle `PUDDLE` descriptor and drip are the witness | sight-glass module-body (corruptible); PUDDLE and DRIP consequence |

271	A WORN descriptor has no row: it is module-body and witnesses nothing. The witness of a worn machine is its falling output through D.4 (`out_scr`, `circ`, lamp brightness via `served_pm`) and, once a hazard mode takes over, that mode's consequence-channel descriptor. A PATCH_WEEP descriptor is on the consequence channel and witnesses the patch itself (`hp_cap < HP_FULL`): the Filter may repaint a patched module as whole, but may neither remove the weep nor add one to a sound module *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*.
272	
273	The headless test: set Perception output to "all OK" for a degraded fixture and assert `state_hash` of `graph.state` at tick N is identical with and without the Perception block's content (the kernel's own `PERCEPTION_OUT` pattern).

275	**LS-23 — Patch, repair, decay.** `repair_step(PATCH)` raises `hp` by its delta up to `hp_cap = min(hp_cap, PATCH_CAP_BP 6000)` and records `patched_at_step`; a patched subject is therefore permanently DEGRADED at sev 1 (a patch weeps: its tell is the consequence-channel PATCH_WEEP of LS-11, not WORN, so a hallucinated "fixed" module cannot hide a failing patch) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* — it works at `eff` 750 and the leak mode is cleared because `hp ≥ LEAK_HP`. After `PATCH_DECAY_STEPS` (2400 = `PATCH_DECAY_S` 240 × 10) the patch decays at `PATCH_DECAY_BP_PER_100` per wear period and re-leaks when `hp` drops below `LEAK_HP` again; the re-leak is endogenous and gated, and the gate is open because the sev-1 PATCH_WEEP descriptor has been live since the patch (R15). `repair_step(FULL)` requires the Item DB part named by `repair_part_for(subject)` (edges have no `def_id`) and restores `hp_cap = HP_FULL`; a PATCH consumes no item *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from item-and-module-database)*. DESTROYED is never repairable; the path is salvage → install. Nothing in the Graph rewards repair: no progression value is written anywhere (brief: no player progression from the Graph).
276	
277	**LS-24 — Invariants, FAULTED tiers, bounded work.** Two tiers, and every invariant in this GDD belongs to one. *Structural (hard):* edge endpoint slot out of range or pointing at a tombstone; array lengths disagree; ids not strictly ascending; `next_id ≤ max id`; CSR inconsistent with edges; a seam sub-edge whose SeamRecord is missing — checked after every topology mutator in debug, in `post_restore` in all builds, every run in debug; a violation is a kernel step-invariant failure → FAULTED (dev halts; release returns to the menu; no autosave). Every check is raised through `GraphFault.raise(code, subject)`, which records the code, returns the failure to the kernel and, in debug, also halts; no invariant relies on GDScript `assert`, which is stripped from release builds and cannot be caught *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. *Numeric (soft):* an amount below 0, a field above its documented max, conservation drift ≠ 0, `ΔT` clamped — in release clamp to range, increment `graph_saturations[field]` and continue; in debug `GraphFault.raise` halts. Every test suite asserts `graph_saturations` is all zeros, so a rounding defect still fails CI without ejecting a player from a 40-minute session. Work per run is bounded by construction (D.16): one pass per loop, `MAX_SPREAD_PER_STEP` failures, `MAX_FOOTPRINTS_PER_STEP` writes, never catch-up; `STEP_BUDGET_MS` (registry 4 ms, "Diagnostic alarm for P3; target is 2 ms") is the kernel's logging threshold, not a cut-off, and the Graph's own budget of record is the **spike share** it asks of that 2 ms target — the sum of the Graph hooks that run on one hook tick at **P99 ≤ 0.5 ms and max ≤ 1.0 ms** on a release export (Godot 4.7.2 release template, `forward_plus`, vsync on, 120-frame warm-up) on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK (delegated ruling R12; `project.yaml` `qa.min_spec`; pending spike measurement; pass needs P99 within the R12 headroom of the frame ceiling) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R12)* — with the allocation, read-side and decision-ladder clauses of D.16; the first draft's "10 ms at 10 Hz" framing was wrong, because the constraint is a spike on one 60 Hz frame in six that every other divisor-6 hook shares, and the technical-director's apportionment of the 2 ms target is Open Question 31 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*.
278	
279	**LS-25 — Endogenous rates: wear, compression, stress.** Everything that damages a subject without a player or a horror doing it is one of: overload (D.9) and the short burn of a FAILED cable in SHORT (D.9) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, wear on period steps (LEAK, OVERHEAT, fatigue, patch decay, and **duty** — `W_DUTY_BP_PER_100` on every running SCRUBBER, PUMP, REACTOR and HEATER, D.9, so that a fully repaired ship is quiet for a session but never permanently safe (P5): at 2 bp per period a healthy machine reaches `HP_OK` after 1500 periods = 4.2 h of continuous duty and carries WORN from then on *(Amended 2026-10-26 — CD-GDD-ALIGN)*), thaw-burst (C5). All of it is multiplied by the section's `rate_pm` (HOME 1000; DERELICT `10^6 / DERELICT_FAULT_COMPRESSION` = 2000, so a derelict fault's wear clock runs at half length; clocks set by a stock draining — a tank emptying, a pool venting — do not compress) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* and by `stress_pm` (`BREACH_PROPAGATION_MULT` 2000 while the section is stressed by M17 STRESS, 1000 otherwise). The multipliers never touch gas exchange, heat conduction or supply: the breach rhythm makes the ship *fail* faster, not *leak* faster — the hole still sets the hiss. On a derelict, faults that are "dead" (dried trails) are authored as subjects at `hp` ≤ `HP_FAIL` with a `def_id` whose module is powered-off, so they emit descriptors with `intensity_pm` 0 and `since_steps` large (the dried trail) and only wake when power or coolant reaches them.

281	**LS-26 — The MVP slice (R23) and what waits.** *Mode count note (consistency check 2026-10-26): "six MVP modes" are six hazard groups — LEAK, SHORT/OVERLOAD, OVERHEAT/SCRAM, FREEZE, BREACH, STARVE — spanning ids 1–7 and 9; SEVERED (8) is also MVP-live by construction because salvage (V8, M6/M12) produces an `open_end`; WORN (10) and SEAL_STRAIN (26) are non-hazard and live wherever hp or a closed hatch exists.* Home-ship (handmade): 5 compartments — cryo bay, corridor, engine room, cargo bay, airlock/pod dock — with all five loops: 1 REACTOR, 1 BATTERY, 2 CABLE_JUNCTIONs with breakers, ~8 LOADs (lamps 20 W at `waste_permille` 1000, door motors, scrubber 600 W at 400 ‰, pump 400 W at 300 ‰, one HEATER 500 W at 1000 ‰ in the cryo bay — the heat budget that keeps the ship at COMFORT, D.15 HEALTHY), ~8 CABLEs; 1 SCRUBBER, 1 O2_TANK (3,000,000 mGU), 5 VENTs, ~5 DUCTs (one exposed, in the cryo bay, authored as a spur so that its FAILED state cuts no vent's `path_cap`, D.15 O2-SHIP) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; 1 RESERVOIR (20,000 mL), 1 PUMP, 1 RADIATOR, 3 PIPEs; 1 FUEL_TANK, 2 FUEL PIPEs; 7 HULL_SEGMENTs (two breachable per outer room); 1 weld socket. ~40 nodes, ~55 edges (all counts in this rule are estimates; Derelict Authoring's templates are of record, e.g. 11 home-ship LOADs) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from derelict-authoring-handmade-kits)*. Derelict A (cold wreck, first sortie — the home-ship is the spawn; registry `mvp_template_roster`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from derelict-authoring-handmade-kits, boarding-and-salvage)*: 4 compartments, dead bus, 1 BATTERY at partial charge, scrubber FAILED (`hp` 2000) to salvage (first V8), one frozen and leaking PIPE, 4 segments; ~30 nodes. Derelict B (hot wreck, second sortie, the weld donor): 5 compartments, live REACTOR in SCRAM, one latent seam fault, a hull breach, coolant leak behind the overheat; ~35 nodes. ≤ 12 compartments at the weld (this bounds the welded body, home + B = 10, not the loaded set {home + B, A} = 14) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from derelict-authoring-handmade-kits, modular-ship-assembly)*. The eight faults, each on a D.15 fixture: O2 pinhole at a clamp (exposed DUCT LEAK — the ship clock), O2 seam leak after weld (`A_seam_m` — the room clock, D.15 SEAM-WEEP), bus overload (PWR-OVL), broken breaker (a CABLE_JUNCTION at `hp` 2000, branch dark until replaced, D.15 BROKEN-BREAKER), coolant leak (CLT-LEAK), pump stall (PUMP STARVE on a dead branch → C3, D.15 PUMP-STALL), fuel flange drip (FUEL-DRIP) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*, hull fatigue → breach (HULL-FATIGUE). Verbs: V1 patch, V3 breaker, V4 bulkhead, V5 valve, V6 emergency vent, V8 salvage, V9 weld, V12 hand crank = M11 `reset_node` only, LS-18 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*, **V7 top-up** — **an MVP verb by user ruling (D34, D40, D70b, X5, 2026-10-27)**: a deliberate, actively chosen O2 tap at a lit port, which reaches the Graph as a Suit-side M16 `withdraw_store` call at the tank port (the Graph's M16 was MVP-live already and gains no rule); Suit runs `TOPUP_MODE` VERB with `CELL_ENABLED` on, so the lamp cell and the Pillar 3 "go dark" lever exist at MVP; Open Question 20 is resolved *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*; modes live: LEAK, SHORT/OVERLOAD, OVERHEAT/SCRAM, FREEZE, BREACH, STARVE (plus WORN on every duty-worn machine and SEAL_STRAIN at the closed seam hatch — both live in MVP by construction, neither a hazard mode; *Amended 2026-10-26 — CD-GDD-ALIGN*). The first fault the player meets is a coolant frost trail from the cryo bay (a coolant PIPE LEAK in a cryo bay authored at `T` −2000 mC, FROST band, so the drip frosts — the art bible's carried element). MVP must prove: C2/C3/C6 readable from the world; one weld joining a derelict (power + air + opening) with physical consequences (weep at the seam, draught when the hatch opens); save v1 round-trip with `state_hash`; the six modes live. **Waits for VS-A:** fire and C9, C10 and STRUT load, HEAT_EXCHANGER, FRAME_NODE, FUEL_PORT, CO2, V2/V10/V11, procedural subgraph templates, multiple reservoirs, footprint kinds beyond the five, quiescence sleeping, compaction and Web Map deltas, the hook stagger, power cycles.

283	### States and Transitions
284	
285	**Node and edge lifecycle.** `state` is evaluated in phase 9 from `hp`, `forced_mode` and the mutators that ran in P2. "Gate" means the D.11 gate for endogenous causes; exogenous causes are never gated.

301	**Mode overlays** (independent of `state` unless they force FAILED): LEAK on/off at `LEAK_HP` (edge: `N/<id>`, `F/<id>` on intensity bucket); OVERLOAD on/off at `ρ` 1000; STARVE on/off at `served_pm` 1000 (status; `N/<id>`); OVERHEAT on after `OVERHEAT_ON_STEPS` above `OVERHEAT_ON_MC`, off below `OVERHEAT_OFF_MC`; FREEZE pre-stage on/off at `FREEZE_WARN_MC`; BREACH on at `hp < BREACH_HP` (gated), off at `hp ≥ BREACH_HP`; SEVERED on by cut/salvage, off by `cap_port`; WORN on while `hp < HP_OK` with no mode 1–9 live and no patch, off otherwise (`N/<id>` only on the state change; module-body channel, LS-14); PATCH_WEEP on while `hp_cap < HP_FULL`, `hp < HP_OK` and no mode 1–9 live (consequence channel, LS-11) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-26 — CD-GDD-ALIGN)*.
302	
303	**Compartment band states** (each of `band_o2`, `band_p`, `band_t` is its own state machine over the LS-7 table; a transition in the worsening direction fires at the boundary, in the improving direction at boundary + `H`; the band held at the end of a run is persisted (LS-21) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; every transition emits `B/<cid>` and the matching `ATMO_*` descriptor severity): NORMAL ⇄ THIN ⇄ HYPOXIC ⇄ ANOXIC; NORMAL ⇄ LOW ⇄ DECOMP ⇄ VACUUM; SCORCH ⇄ HOT ⇄ COMFORT ⇄ COOL ⇄ FROST ⇄ FREEZING ⇄ DEEP_COLD. Transitions are driven only by phases 4–7 and M15/M17 CHILL/BURN; a band never changes on a tick where no Graph hook ran. `pressure_trend` is derived, not a state.
304	
305	**Seam states.** `ACTIVE` (created by M2 with every sub-edge disconnected; weeps per D.2; sub-edges opened by M8/M9/M13) → `ACTIVE` with `leak_bp` 0 after wear-in or a seam PATCH (M7; V11 in VS-A) → `CUT` (M3; SeamRecord kept as a tombstone with the boundary mode; sub-edges tombstoned; `S/<seam_id>` + `T`). A seam's sub-edges carry their own LS-10 lifecycle (a seam CABLE can overload and fail like any cable); the SeamRecord's `hp` is the hull-side seam integrity that D.2's BREACH reads.
306	
307	**Block states.** `EMPTY` (`default_state()`: no sections, counters at 1, `last_step_no` 0) → `LIVE` (after M1 or a successful restore; hooks run; mutators accept) → `RESTORING` (two-phase restore into scratch; the live block is untouched until the swap; `GRAPH_RESTORE_*` on failure leaves it LIVE with the pre-restore state) → `FAULTED` (kernel state after a structural invariant failure in any build or a numeric `GraphFault` in debug: hooks and mutators stop, the kernel owns the exit — dev halt or release-to-menu with no autosave; the partial writes of the failing apply are left in place for the diagnostic dump). The Graph never transitions itself out of FAULTED; a new world or a restore of the last good snapshot does.

309	### Interactions with Other Systems
310	
311	| System | Data in (to the Graph) | Data out (from the Graph) | Interface owner | Hook / `after:` ordering | Status |
312	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
313	| Command & Simulation Layer (kernel) | `WriteScope`, `rng_derive`, tick `T`, dirty-key sink, restore calls | block registration, three hooks, `canonical_bytes()`, `block_hash()` | kernel (CR-3, CR-8, CR-9); K-1 and the D.10 note are routed amendments | hooks at divisor 6, offsets 0 / 2 / 4 (baseline stagger), chained *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | designed; row-1 "Blocks" → "Block" routed |
314	| Item & Module Database | module defs: `node_kind`, `ports[]` by port-type id, `cap`, `tier`, `req_w`, `hp_start`, `waste_permille`; repair part ids | `SalvageRecord{def_id, hp, state, hp_cap, patched_at_step}` on M6 (read by `salvage_yield`); `def_id` validation at restore; `cap_seam` (D.14) callable as a pure function at data load for the Item DB F-12 lint | Item DB consumes the LS-4 ids; the Graph owns them (ADR-LSG-08). 335	## Formulas
336	
337	*Scope note.* Every formula below is integer arithmetic over the fields of `graph.state` and the immutable tuning table `GraphTuning`; nothing here reads Attention, sanity, rhythm state or any `PERCEPTION_OUT` value (LS-21 — a formula whose inputs include any of those is a Pillar 4 violation, not a tuning choice). **Every numeric default is provisional until spikes S0–S3 and the MVP playtest** (Section H); the time-band figures in D.15 are the acceptance targets the defaults were tuned to, not the other way round. Units are the R1 game units: gas in mGU (`GAS_SCALE` 1000 mGU per GU; 1 GU is the amount that gives 0.1 kPa in a 1-tile volume), volume in tiles, pressure derived in dkPa (standard `STD_PRESSURE_DKPA` 1000, standard O2 partial pressure `STD_O2_PP_DKPA` 210), temperature in mC, power in W which is identically dJ per step, energy in dJ, liquids in mL, integrity in basis points 0..10000, fractions in permille, and — on the gas-flow path only — opening area in milli flow units (`A_m` = 1000 × flow units) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. One step is `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` = 6 ticks = 0.1 s at `TICK_RATE` 60; "per step" is the only rate anywhere in this section. Source column vocabulary follows the kernel GDD: `constant` = compiled, changing it is a code change; `data file` = read at boot from `assets/data/life_support_graph.json` into `GraphTuning` (a balance pass edits the file, not the code; a designer-authored float is converted once at boot by `int(round(x × scale))` and never hashed); `calculated` = derived at runtime and never persisted; `state` = a persisted field of `graph.state` (hashed, replicated by summary); `registry` = a locked cross-system fact cited verbatim from `design/registry/entities.yaml`. Three arithmetic rules hold everywhere and are not repeated per formula: (1) **every flux is a non-negative magnitude with an explicit direction**, so integer division is applied only to non-negative operands and truncation is `floor` — written `⌊x⌋`; where a ceiling is wanted it is written `⌈x⌉` and computed as `(num + den − 1) / den` on non-negative operands; the only signed divisions are the two remainder-carrying thermal steps (D.7, D.8), which truncate toward zero and carry the remainder so nothing is lost; (2) **no `sqrt`, `exp`, `pow` or `sin` on the propagation path** — D.15 uses `ln` because it is a design-time estimate evaluated by the test harness, never by the sim; (3) every product the propagation code forms appears in D.13's table with its operand maxima, and the boot assertion there refuses to start a build whose table violates `max_a × max_b < 2^62`.
338	
339	**D.1 Opening gas flow — mGU moved through one opening per step**
340	
341	The `opening_gas_flow` formula is defined as:
342	
343	`g = n_a × V_b − n_b × V_a` (signed, exact; gas moves from `a` to `b` when `g > 0`, from `b` to `a` when `g < 0`, not at all when `g = 0`) ; `Δn = min( ⌊G_OPEN × A_m × abs(g) / (V_a × V_b × GAS_SCALE × 1000)⌋ , ⌊abs(g) / ((V_a + V_b) × deg_max)⌋ )` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
344	
345	Derived: `abs(g) / (V_a × V_b × GAS_SCALE)` is the exact pressure difference in dkPa, so the first term is `G_OPEN × A × ΔP` with `A = A_m / 1000` and the second is the old equalising amount over the degree; the floored `P_a`, `P_b` of D.3 serve bands, display and dirty-key quanta only and **never enter a flux**, so a floor can neither reverse the flux near balance nor break the monotone-gradient property of D.12 (the first draft took `ΔP` from the floored values and could)
346	Derived: when the lower side is EXTERIOR (`P_EXT` = 0), the first term is `⌊G_OPEN × A_m × n_tot_src / (V_src × GAS_SCALE × 1000)⌋`, the second is `⌊n_tot_src / deg_src⌋` and `Δn` is added to the source section's `vented_mgu`
347	Derived: species split `Δn_o2 = ⌊Δn × n_o2_src / n_tot_src⌋` (0 when `n_tot_src` = 0), `Δn_inert = Δn − Δn_o2`
348	Derived: per-step fraction `k = G_OPEN × A / (V_src × GAS_SCALE)` — the single number every time-to-band estimate in D.15 is built from
349	
350	**Variables:**
351	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
352	|----------|------|-------|--------|-------------|
353	| G_OPEN | int | 1–10 (default **2**) | data file | mGU moved per (area unit × dkPa × step); the decompression-speed knob |
354	| A_m | int | 0–512,000 (door 64,000; pinhole 1,000; a seam weep may be any value ≥ 1) | state (`area` × 1000 of a stored OPENING) or calculated (D.2: `A_hole` × 1000, or the seam weep `A_seam_m`) | Opening area in milli flow units (1000 = one flow unit = 1/64 of a door aperture, LS-5) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
355	| P_a, P_b | int | 0–1500 dkPa | calculated (D.3, from the start-of-phase snapshot) | Floored display pressures on each side (bands, `AIRFLOW` intensity, D.12); EXTERIOR reads `P_EXT` = 0 (R14); **not an input of `Δn`** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
356	| V_a, V_b | int | 4–200 tiles | state (cached from Layout, LS-6) | Volumes |
357	| GAS_SCALE | int | 1000 | constant (registry candidate) | mGU per GU |
358	| deg_max | int | 1–16 | calculated (topology refresh) | `max(deg_a, deg_b)` where `deg` counts the OPENING edges and virtual holes of a compartment with area > 0; EXTERIOR counts as degree 1 — the D.12 stability divisor |
359	| n_a, n_b, n_o2_src, n_tot_src | int | 0–`n_max(c)` = `P_MAX` × `V` × `GAS_SCALE` (≤ 3×10^8 mGU) | state | Gas amounts and composition of the two compartments at the start of the phase *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
360	| g | int | −6×10^10..+6×10^10 | calculated | Exact signed gradient `n_a × V_b − n_b × V_a` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
361	| Δn | int | 0–`n_tot_src` | calculated | mGU moved this step |
362	
363	**Output Range:** 0 to the equalisation amount divided by the degree; it never overshoots (the second term is the amount that would exactly equalise two finite volumes, or everything the room holds against vacuum) and it never goes negative (magnitude with direction); the sign of the flux is always the sign of the true gradient `g`, even when both rooms read the same floored dkPa *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. It is 0 when `A_m` = 0, when `g` = 0, and — the truncation bias TD required this document to state — whenever `G_OPEN × A × ΔP < 1`: **equalisation stalls within `⌈1/k⌉` mGU** of the exact balance, which for a pinhole (`A` = 1, `V` = 20) is 10,000 mGU = 0.5 dkPa in that room and for a door is 156 mGU. This is expected behaviour, not a defect: the residual is below the 10 dkPa dirty-key quantum and below anything a gauge or a lung can register. Maximum for a door at full vacuum: `2 × 64 × 1000` = 128,000 mGU/step (a 20-tile room empties through an open hatch in about 160 steps = 16 s; LOW band in 5.6 s — the "chaos" end of the scale, Section C LS-7). The model is linear and unchoked: a vent through a hole slows as the pressure falls, which is the readable behaviour (the hiss fades as the room dies) and the reason no table or square-root law is needed.
364	**Example:** room a (`V_a` = 20, `P_a` = 1000, `n_tot` = 20,000,000, `n_o2` = 4,200,000, `deg_a` = 2) to room b (`V_b` = 40, `P_b` = 400, `deg_b` = 3) through a door `A` = 64: `g` = 20,000,000 × 40 − 16,000,000 × 20 = 480,000,000 (exact `ΔP` 600); first term `2 × 64,000 × 480,000,000 / (20 × 40 × 1000 × 1000)` = 76,800; second term `480,000,000 / (60 × 3)` = 2,666,666; `Δn` = 76,800; `Δn_o2` = `⌊76,800 × 4,200,000 / 20,000,000⌋` = 16,128; `Δn_inert` = 60,672. After the step `n_a` = 19,923,200 → `P_a` = `⌊19,923,200 / 20,000⌋` = 996; `n_b` = 16,000,000 + 76,800 → `P_b` = `⌊16,076,800 / 40,000⌋` = 401. Pinhole to vacuum from the same room: `Δn` = `min(⌊2 × 1,000 × 20,000,000 / (20 × 1000 × 1000)⌋, ⌊20,000,000 / 2⌋)` = 2,000 mGU/step, `k` = 0.0001 per step.

371

531	**Output Range:** `T` is bounded below by `T_amb` (the plate term stops within `⌈100000 / (K_HULL × S_ext)⌉` mC of it — 182 mC for the example room: the thermal truncation stall, expected) and above by the balance between `Q_src_room` and the loss terms, `ΔT_eq = Q_src_room / (K_HULL × S_ext / 100 + K_HOLE × Σ A_hole)` °C above ambient. The plate time constant `τ = 100 × C / (K_HULL × S_ext)` is 16,364 steps = 27 min for the example room on its own — a sealed, unheated room is a slow cold — but a hole of area `A` adds `K_HOLE × A` dJ/°C to a plate conductance of only 5.5, so a RUPTURE hole (`A` 7) cuts `τ` to 4,615 steps and a breached room reaches FROST in 3.9 min and freezes its pipes in 12 min (D.15), which is the cold the player meets. **The healthy baseline is the constraint these defaults were set to:** the MVP home-ship (Σ `S_ext` 80 → 20 dJ/°C of plate loss) keeps every compartment in COMFORT on one 500 W heater plus lamp, scrubber and pump waste (≈ 1,020 dJ/step → about 21 °C uniform against a −30 °C sink, with `K_OPEN` 4 moving 640 dJ/step per 10 °C across each open door); an earlier draft at `K_HULL` ≡ 1 dJ and `T_amb` −40000 lost 1,320 dJ/step per outer room and would have held a *healthy* engine room in FREEZING with its pipes' pre-stage permanently lit — a constantly warning healthy ship, which P1 and P2 forbid. With the heater off (power loss) the whole ship cools with `τ_ship` ≈ 15,000 steps: breath fog at 6 min, frost at 13 min, and — with no hole at all — its liquid pipes show the FREEZE pre-stage at 23 min and freeze solid at 41 min (D.15 SHIP-COLD, the intentional dark-ship clock): the dark is cold and, given time, freezing, and a breach or a derelict brings it forward to 12 min, which is why `T_amb` is −30000 (a sink only 10 °C below `FREEZE_ON_MC`, the Section G build assertion) and not deeper *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. Energy is conserved exactly: `Σ U + radiated_dj × 1000` over a section is constant when no machine runs, because every `Q_open` is subtracted once and added once and every `Q_hull` is counted into `radiated_dj`. The remainder is carried, never dropped, so a room 0.5 °C from equilibrium still moves (the stall above is from the hull term's own floor, not from the step). **Thermostat** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: the first draft's heater was a fixed 500 W with no thermostat, so closing doors — the main decompression response — left the heater room with nowhere to put its heat and it reached HOT in about 8 min, a healthy ship starting to warn because the player did the right thing (P1, P2). With the thermostat the heater room settles where `500 × duty_t` equals its loss, just under `T_SET_MC` (a sealed 42-tile cryo bay about 21.3 °C), and the HEALTHY uniform equilibrium of the open ship moves from 21 °C to about 20 °C (heater duty ≈ 0.96). The `MAX_DT` saturation of a heater in a 4-tile closet (41 mC per step at full request) is still a content bug, but the room can no longer be driven past `T_SET_MC` by the heater.
532	**Example:** `V` = 30 → `C` = 90,000; `S_ext` = 22; `T` = 40,000; `T_amb` = −30,000; `Q_src_room` = 516 (D.8 example); `t_rem` = 12,500; no openings or holes. `Q_hull` = `⌊25 × 22 × 70,000 / 100,000⌋` = 385 outward; `Q_net` = 516 − 385 = 131; `E` = 12,500 + 131,000 = 143,500; `ΔT` = `trunc(143,500 / 90,000)` = 1; `t_rem'` = 143,500 − 90,000 = 53,500; `T'` = 40,001; `radiated_dj` += 385. Check: `U` before = 40,000 × 90,000 + 12,500 = 3,600,012,500; after = 40,001 × 90,000 + 53,500 = 3,600,143,500; difference 131,000 = 1000 × (516 − 385) exactly. With a RUPTURE hole (`A` 7) in the same room the hole term adds `⌊2 × 7 × 70,000 / 1000⌋` = 980, `Q_net` = −849, and the room cools 9 mC per step.
533	
534	**D.8 Coolant circulation, heat capture, radiator and the machine temperature proxy**
535	
536	The `coolant_loop` formula is defined as:
537	
538	`lvl_f = clamp( (level_pm − L_CAV_LO) × 1000 / (L_CAV_HI − L_CAV_LO) , 0 , 1000 )` ; `circ = ⌊pump_eff × sat × lvl_f / 10^6⌋` ; `Q_cap = min( Q_src , ⌊K_CAP × circ × max(0, T_room − t_cool) / 10^6⌋ )`
539	
540	Derived: radiator `Q_rad = ⌊K_RAD × eff_r × circ × max(0, t_cool − T_amb_r) / 10^9⌋`, added to the section's `radiated_dj`
541	Derived: coolant temperature `E_c = tc_rem + 1000 × (Σ Q_cap − Σ Q_rad)`; `Δt_cool = trunc(E_c / (C_COOL × level_ml))`; `tc_rem' = E_c − Δt_cool × C_COOL × level_ml` (with `level_ml` ≥ 1; at 0 the reservoir carries no heat and `Q_cap` is already 0)
542	Derived: uncaptured heat `Q_src_room = Q_src − Q_cap` enters the machine's compartment (D.7)
543	Derived: machine temperature proxy `T_mach = T_room + ⌊Q_src_room × K_MACH⌋` — the OVERHEAT trigger (LS-11) and the HOT/shimmer pre-stage that opens the fairness window before a SCRAM
544	Derived: `circ` through a path is 0 when any PIPE on it is FAILED (cap 0), any VALVE closed, or the PUMP's node is not OK/DEGRADED; `level_pm = ⌊1000 × level_ml / cap_ml⌋`
545	Derived (guards) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: a RESERVOIR with `cap_ml` 0 reads `level_pm` 0 (`circ` 0, no division); `L_CAV_LO ≥ L_CAV_HI` refuses to boot; a PIPE leak debits the reservoir in the same phase 5 before `level_pm` is read, in ascending reservoir id
546	
547	**Variables:**
548	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
549	|----------|------|-------|--------|-------------|
550	| level_ml, cap_ml | int | 0–cap_ml / 5,000–100,000 (default 20,000) | state / data file (module def) | Reservoir fill and rated capacity |
551	| L_CAV_LO, L_CAV_HI | int | 0–399 / 401–1000, LO < HI asserted at boot (defaults 200 / 600) | data file | Below LO the pump cavitates (circ 0); above HI full circulation; the `lvl_f` denominator is `max(1, L_CAV_HI − L_CAV_LO)` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
552	| pump_eff, sat | int | 0–1000 | calculated (D.4, D.6 tier 1) | Pump integrity and power |
553	| circ | int | 0–1000 ‰ | calculated | Circulation fraction |
554	| Q_src | int | 0–4000 dJ/step | calculated | Waste heat the jacketed machine produces: `⌊out_w × waste_permille / 1000⌋` |
555	| K_CAP | int | 20–150 (default 75) dJ/step/°C | data file | Jacket coupling |
556	| K_RAD | int | 20–150 (default 60) | data file | Radiator coupling |
557	| eff_r | int | 0–1000 | calculated (D.4) | Radiator integrity |
558	| T_room, t_cool, T_amb_r | int | mC | state / state / data file (`T_AMB_MC`) | Machine room, coolant and radiator-face temperatures |
559	| C_COOL | int | 2–8 (default 4) dJ/°C per mL | data file | Coolant thermal mass per mL |
560	| tc_rem | int | ±(C_COOL × level_ml) | state | Carried remainder |
561	| K_MACH | int | 10–100 (default 40) mC per dJ/step | data file | How far a machine's casing runs above its room per unit of uncaptured heat |
562	| T_mach | int | mC | calculated | Machine proxy temperature |
563	
564	**Output Range:** `circ` 0..1000; `Q_cap ≤ Q_src`; heat not captured stays in the room and in the machine's casing, so losing coolant makes the engine room climb through HOT (1,500 dJ/step against 5.5 dJ/°C of plate loss would head for SCORCH, but door conduction at `K_OPEN` 4 spreads it and the SCRAM below cuts it within 35 s) and the reactor casing hot: at `circ` = 0 with `Q_src` = 1500 and `K_MACH` = 40, `T_mach` = `T_room + 60,000` = 80 °C from a 20 °C room — above `OVERHEAT_ON_MC` 70000, so a stalled pump or a cut coolant line leads to OVERHEAT (sev 3, scorch and shimmer at the casing) and after `OVERHEAT_SCRAM_STEPS` to SCRAM. The pre-stage is continuous: between `L_CAV_HI` and `L_CAV_LO` the capture falls linearly and `T_mach` climbs through HOT (40,000..69,999, sev 2 shimmer) before it reaches OVERHEAT — the player sees the casing sweat for minutes before it scorches. Radiator output always goes to `radiated_dj`, so section energy is exactly accounted.

565	**Example:** `level_ml` = 11,000 of 20,000 (`level_pm` = 550), `pump_eff` = 1000, `sat` = 1000 → `lvl_f` = `350 × 1000 / 400` = 875 → `circ` = 875. `Q_src` = 1500, `T_room` = 40,000, `t_cool` = 25,000, `K_CAP` = 75 → `Q_cap` = `min(1500, ⌊75 × 875 × 15,000 / 10^6⌋)` = `min(1500, 984)` = 984; `Q_src_room` = 516 (used in D.7); `T_mach` = 40,000 + 516 × 40 = 60,640 (HOT, below OVERHEAT). Radiator `K_RAD` = 60, `eff_r` = 1000, `T_amb_r` = −30,000 → `Q_rad` = `⌊60 × 1000 × 875 × 55,000 / 10^9⌋` = 2887. `E_c` = `0 + 1000 × (984 − 2887)` = −1,903,000; `C_COOL × level_ml` = 44,000 → `Δt_cool` = −43; `tc_rem'` = −1,903,000 + 1,892,000 = −11,000; the coolant cools toward the point where rejection equals the capped capture (about −1.4 °C for this reactor at `circ` 875), which is the designed steady state — and at full circulation on a healthy loop the capture is the full `Q_src`, so a healthy engine room receives only its pump's and lamps' waste.
566	
567	**D.9 Overload, wear and the damage multipliers — every endogenous hp loss**
568	
569	The `endogenous_damage` formula is defined as:
570	
571	`ρ = ⌊1000 × load / cap⌋` ; `Δhp_ovl = min( DHP_MAX , ⌊OVL_K × max(0, ρ − 1000)² / 10^4⌋ )` per step ; `Δhp_wear = W_base` on steps where `step_no mod WEAR_PERIOD_STEPS = 0`, else 0 ; `Δhp = ⌊(Δhp_ovl + Δhp_wear + Δhp_short) × rate_pm × stress_pm / 10^6⌋` with `Δhp_short = SHORT_BURN_BP_PER_STEP` on every step (not only period steps) while the guard below holds *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*
572	
573	Derived: `W_base` is the sum of the wear terms that apply to the subject: `LEAK_WEAR_BP_PER_100` while in mode LEAK because `hp < LEAK_HP` **and** its descriptor's `intensity_pm > 0` (the seam weep is a geometry-driven mode-1 descriptor at `hp` ≥ `LEAK_HP` and carries **no** LEAK wear, so a default seam never ends below `HP_OK` with a permanent pre-stage *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*) (an isolated leak behind a closed valve draws from nothing and holds its `hp`; re-opened, it resumes from the stored `hp`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from derelict-authoring-handmade-kits)*; `HEAT_WEAR_BP_PER_100` while in mode OVERHEAT; `HULL_FATIGUE_BP_PER_100` while a HULL_SEGMENT's `fatigued` flag is set; `PATCH_DECAY_BP_PER_100` while `hp_cap < HP_FULL` and `step_no − patched_at_step ≥ PATCH_DECAY_STEPS`; **duty wear** `⌈W_DUTY_BP_PER_100 × duty_pm / 1000⌉` on a SCRUBBER, PUMP, HEATER or REACTOR in state OK or DEGRADED while `duty_pm > 0` (a RADIATOR only if its module def sets `duty_wear` true — off in MVP), where `duty_pm` = `run_pm` (LS-19) — `served_pm` for a SCRUBBER or PUMP whose request is above 0, `⌊duty_t × served_pm / 1000⌋` for a HEATER (its `req_w` stays 500 while the thermostat is satisfied, so `served_pm` alone would wear an idle heater at full rate), `⌊1000 × out_w / out_w_rated⌋` for the REACTOR, and 0 for any machine whose request is 0 (a pump at `throttle_pm` 0, a thermostat-satisfied heater, a reactor at `out_w` 0) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* — the ceiling means a machine that runs at all wears at least 1 bp per period *(Amended 2026-10-26 — CD-GDD-ALIGN: no safe harbour, P5)*
574	Derived: `rate_pm = 1000` for a HOME section, `10^6 / DERELICT_FAULT_COMPRESSION` = 2000 for a DERELICT section; `stress_pm = BREACH_PROPAGATION_MULT` while `step_no < stress_until_step`, else 1000
575	Derived (cause tag) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: overload damage taken during the `INRUSH_STEPS` after a breaker close (M9, the branch's `energised_at_step`) is tagged EXOGENOUS — a breaker closed onto an overload is a player verb (R7) — and bypasses the D.11 gate; after that window the same overload is ENDOGENOUS and gated
576	Derived *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: the result is applied as `Δhp_applied = min( Δhp , max(0, hp − floor_hp) )` and `hp' = hp − Δhp_applied` — the floor **limits the reduction and can never raise `hp`** (the first draft's `hp' = max(hp − Δhp, floor_hp)` healed a plate ruptured to 3600 back up to 4000 on the same run, and lifted any gouge below `HP_FAIL` to 3001). While the D.11 gate is closed, `floor_hp` is `BREACH_HP` for a HULL_SEGMENT or SEAM whose `hp ≥ BREACH_HP` (the LEAK → BREACH escalation is gated), otherwise `HP_FAIL + 1` for a subject above `HP_FAIL`, and `1` for a subject already FAILED (the gated FAILED → DESTROYED case); once the gate is open it is 0. A subject already below its floor takes no further endogenous damage until the gate opens and is never moved; `Δhp` never carries over — damage discarded by the gate is gone
577	Derived (guard) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; short burn added 2026-10-27 — re-review, carried-over blocker: the guard alone stopped all damage at FAILED)*: `ρ` is evaluated only for a CABLE (or seam CABLE) with `cap` > 0, so `ρ` never divides by 0; a FAILED or DESTROYED cable has `cap` 0, carries no load (the island re-splits, C1) and takes no *overload* damage. **Short burn:** a FAILED CABLE that is still in mode SHORT (LS-11) keeps burning — `Δhp_short` = `SHORT_BURN_BP_PER_STEP` on every step — while an island at either of its ends holds a live source (`S + D` > 0). Without it the clock stops at FAILED (2.9 min), a cable can never reach DESTROYED, and the PWR-OVL fixture, its criteria and the R21 power band (3.8–5.2 min) are unreachable. The burn is inside the `rate_pm` and `stress_pm` multiplier and under the D.11 gate (floor 1 for a FAILED subject while the gate is closed; by then the gate has been open for ≥ 100 steps); the player stops it by opening the upstream breaker (M9: the island at that end then has no live source) or by repair; it never applies to a CABLE_JUNCTION or LOAD (a static BROKEN-BREAKER fault does not burn itself out) or to an authored dead cable with no source behind it. 4 bp per step is 400 bp per 100 steps: the FAILED → DESTROYED leg of PWR-OVL is `3000 / 4` = 750 steps. (The first re-review's suggested `SHORT_WEAR` of 70 bp per period was wrong: 3000 → 0 in 750 steps needs about 400 per 100 steps.)
578	
579	**Variables:**
580	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
581	|----------|------|-------|--------|-------------|
582	| load, cap | int | 0–20000 / 500–6000 W | calculated (tree flow, D.6) / state (post D.14 for seams) | Power carried / rated |
583	| ρ | int | 0–40000 ‰ | calculated | Utilisation |
584	| OVL_K | int | 1–16 (default 4) | data file | Overload damage scale |
585	| DHP_MAX | int | 500–5000 (default 2000) bp | data file | Arc-flash clamp per step |
586	| SHORT_BURN_BP_PER_STEP | int | 1–40 (default **4** = 400 bp per 100 steps) | data file; ★ registry candidate | Burn of a FAILED cable still in mode SHORT with a live source behind it (guard above); sets the FAILED → DESTROYED leg of D.15 PWR-OVL *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* |
587	| WEAR_PERIOD_STEPS | int | 50–200 (default 100) steps | data file | Wear is applied once per period (10 s) — the groan-and-tick cadence the player hears |
588	| LEAK_WEAR_BP_PER_100 | int | 0–100 (default **16**) | data file | A leaking fitting erodes |
589	| HEAT_WEAR_BP_PER_100 | int | 0–200 (default 40) | data file | An overheating machine cooks itself |
590	| HULL_FATIGUE_BP_PER_100 | int | 0–200 (default **50**) | data file | A fatigued plate creeps toward breach |
591	| PATCH_DECAY_BP_PER_100 | int | 0–500 (default 100) | data file | A decayed patch lets go |
592	| PATCH_DECAY_STEPS | int | 600–6000 (default **2400** = `PATCH_DECAY_S` 240 × 10) | data file (derived from registry candidate `PATCH_DECAY_S`) | How long a patch holds before it starts to decay |
593	| W_DUTY_BP_PER_100 | int | 1–6 (default **2**) | data file (registry candidate `W_DUTY_BP_PER_100`) | Duty wear per period on a running machine at full duty *(Amended 2026-10-26 — CD-GDD-ALIGN)*: at 2 bp per 100 steps a healthy machine loses 720 bp per hour (7.2 %/h) and crosses `HP_OK` after `⌈3000 / 2⌉` = 1500 periods = 150,000 steps = 4.17 h of continuous duty, `HP_FAIL` after 3500 periods = 9.7 h — quiet for a session, never permanently safe |
594	| duty_pm | int | 0–1000 ‰ | calculated (`run_pm`, LS-19: D.6 `served_pm` of a consumer with a non-zero request; HEATER `⌊duty_t × served_pm / 1000⌋`; REACTOR `⌊1000 × out_w / out_w_rated⌋`; 0 when switched off) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | How hard the machine ran this period *(Amended 2026-10-26 — CD-GDD-ALIGN)* |
595	| DERELICT_FAULT_COMPRESSION | int | 250–1000 (default **500** ‰) | data file (registry candidate) | Derelict time-band compression; 500 ‰ doubles the wear rate |
596	| BREACH_PROPAGATION_MULT | int | 1000–3000 (default **2000** ‰) | data file (registry candidate) | Phase-C multiplier applied while a section is stressed (M17 STRESS) |
597	| stress_until_step | int | ≥ 0 | state (per section) | Set by M17 STRESS to `step_no + STRESS_HOLD_STEPS` (default 600 = 60 s) |
598	| Δhp | int | 0–6000 | calculated | hp lost this step |
599	
600	**Output Range:** `Δhp_ovl` is 0 for `ρ ≤ 1000`, 1 bp/step at `ρ` = 1050, 4 at 1100, 16 at 1200, 64 at 1400, clamped at 2000 (`ρ` ≥ 3236). Short burn is 4 bp per step on a HOME section (8 on a DERELICT section) once a cable is FAILED in SHORT with a live source behind it, until the breaker is opened *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. Wear is coarse by design: hp falls in visible lumps every 10 s (50 bp for a fatigued plate), so the tell has a rhythm, not a creep. Duty wear is the floor under that rhythm *(Amended 2026-10-26 — CD-GDD-ALIGN)*: 2 bp per period on every running machine is 360 bp over a 30-minute session (a healthy machine ends it at `hp` 9640, still OK, no descriptor — the HEALTHY criterion in Section H) and 720 bp per hour, so `HP_OK` falls at 4.2 h and the machine carries a WORN sev-1 descriptor from then on; a fully repaired ship is therefore quiet for a session and never permanently safe (P5), and because the term is inside `W_base` it is doubled on a DERELICT section and under STRESS like every other wear. The multipliers scale only **endogenous damage** — never D.1 gas physics, D.7 heat or D.5 supply (P1: a stressed ship fails faster; its air does not leave faster than the hole allows). With `rate_pm` 2000 and `stress_pm` 2000 the maximum product is ×4; the overload term at `DHP_MAX` under ×4 is 8000 bp, which is the "6000" ceiling of `Δhp` only after the gate: in practice no subject loses more than its remaining hp. The gate floor at `HP_FAIL + 1` is what makes every endogenous failure arrive at least 10 s after its first trace, whatever the rate *(Amended 2026-10-26 — CD-GDD-ALIGN)*.
601	**Example:** cable `cap` = 3000 carrying 3300 W → `ρ` = 1100 → `Δhp_ovl` = `⌊4 × 100² / 10^4⌋` = 4 bp/step on a HOME section: DEGRADED (hp < 7000) at step 750 (75 s: box glows, hum climbs), FAILED (cap 0, branch dark) at 1750 (2.9 min), DESTROYED at 2500 (4.2 min) — the R21 power band; from step 1750 the cable is FAILED in SHORT with the reactor's island behind it, so it burns on at 4 bp per step (short burn) for the last 3000 bp, 750 steps *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. The same overload on a DERELICT section (`rate_pm` 2000) is 8 bp/step → branch dark in 1.5 min (step 875) and DESTROYED at step 1250. With the upstream breaker opened at step 1760 the cable holds `hp` 2960 and is never DESTROYED. A fatigued hull plate at `hp` 6999: 50 bp per 100 steps → `hp` 3999 after 60 periods = 6000 steps = 10 min (6999 − 3000; it never reads exactly 4000), at which instant D.2 opens a 1-area pinhole *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. A coolant pipe at `hp` 3800 in LEAK: 16 bp per 100 steps → FAILED after `⌈800 / 16⌉` = 50 periods = 8.3 min. Duty *(Amended 2026-10-26 — CD-GDD-ALIGN)*: a SCRUBBER at `hp` 10000 with `served_pm` 1000 loses `⌈2 × 1000 / 1000⌉` = 2 bp on every period step and reads `hp` 6998 — DEGRADED, WORN sev 1, `eff` 999 — on period 1501, step 150,100 = 4.17 h; the same scrubber in a brownout at `served_pm` 400 loses `⌈2 × 400 / 1000⌉` = 1 bp per period and takes 8.3 h.
602	
603	**D.10 Dirty-key budget per step — confirms `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS`**
604	
605	The `dirty_key_budget` formula is defined as:
606	
607	`K_step = C_q + B + N_t + F_c + L_q + S + T_f` with the invariant `K_step ≤ MAX_DIRTY_KEYS`, else the kernel collapses the notification to `ALL`
608	
609	Derived: a continuous value contributes to `C_q`, `F_c` or `L_q` only when `⌊value / quantum⌋` differs from the last-emitted bucket; quanta: `T` 1000 mC, `P` 10 dkPa, `p_o2` 5 dkPa, store/charge 20 ‰, descriptor intensity 100 ‰, `hp` 250 bp
610	Derived: one key per compartment per step (`C/<cid>`), one per band change (`B/<cid>`), one per node or edge state, forced-mode or severity transition (`N/<id>`), one per descriptor intensity bucket change (`F/<id>`), one per loop component summary quantum (`L/<loop>/<anchor>`), one per seam (`S/<seam_id>`), plus `T` and `SEC/<section_id>` for structural change; keys are encoded as `(KIND << 32) | id` ints (LS-20)
611	
612	**Variables:**
613	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
614	|----------|------|-------|--------|-------------|
615	| C_q | int | 0–C | calculated | Compartments that crossed a quantum |
616	| B | int | 0–3C | calculated | Band changes |
617	| N_t | int | 0–N+E | calculated | Node/edge transitions |
618	| F_c | int | 0–F | calculated | Descriptor intensity bucket changes |
619	| L_q | int | 0–components | calculated | Loop summaries that crossed 20 ‰ |
620	| S, T_f | int | 0–seams / 0–1 | calculated | Seam keys; topology flag |
621	| MAX_DIRTY_KEYS | int | 256 | registry (`MAX_DIRTY_KEYS`, "keys per block per tick"; "Above this a notification collapses to ALL") | Kernel constant — this formula confirms it, it does not set it |
622	
623	**Output Range:** steady state 0–3 keys per step (a `T` drifting 7 mC/step crosses a 1000 mC quantum once per ~143 steps; a pinhole's `P` crosses a 10 dkPa quantum once per ~100 steps). Worst designed cascade: MVP (`C` = 12) `12 + 3 + 6 + 8 + 7 + 1 + 1` = 38; VS-A (`C` = 48) `48 + 12 + 20 + 30 + 20 + 4 + 1` = 135 — both under 256; the MVP figure is far under the 128 floor below which this document asks the kernel never to go, while VS-A's 135 is above it, so VS-A relies on 256 and not on the floor *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. Structural events (weld, cut, instantiate, discard) use `T` + `SEC/<id>` only; a derelict instantiation legitimately collapses to `ALL` and the Projector rebuilds. The S1 spike reports keys-per-run percentiles against a P95 ≤ 32 steady-state target.
624	**Example:** the step a reactor SCRAMs: `N_t` = 1 (reactor) + 6 (loads to STARVE), `L_q` = 2 (power and O2 component summaries), `F_c` = 3, `C_q` = 1 → 13 keys.
625	
626	**D.11 Fairness gate — `warn_elapsed` and `alarm_eligible`**
627	
628	The `fairness_gate` formula is defined as:
629

749	`t_leak = ⌈ ln( (n_0 + R_B / k) / (n_band + R_B / k) ) / k ⌉` steps for a compartment losing gas at fraction `k` per step (D.1) and breathing `R_B` mGU/step, with `n_band = p_band × V × GAS_SCALE`

At the first draft's coefficients (1.0 / 2.0 / 3.0 µs) that is `75 × 1.0 + 100 × 2.0 + 10 × 3.0` = 305 µs plus a worst cascade `32 × 1 + 38 × 0.5` = 51 µs ≈ 0.36 ms. The performance review's realistic coefficients (5 / 10 / 15 µs for typed GDScript with array indexing and bounds checks) give `75 × 5 + 100 × 10 + 10 × 15` = 1,525 µs plus a cascade of about 0.2 ms ≈ **1.7 ms, in a plausible range of 0.5–2.5 ms** — against a 2 ms target for the whole tick that every other divisor-6 hook (Suit vitals, Attention, Emitter) also draws on. The first draft's framing "10 ms at 10 Hz" was wrong: the Graph does not spend its time evenly over a 10 ms window, it spends it on one 60 Hz frame in six, and a 1.7 ms spike on a 16.7 ms frame is a frame-time hitch, not a budget saving. That is why the ladder above exists and why S1, not this arithmetic, gates approval: at offsets 0 / 2 / 4 the spike on one tick is the largest single hook (about 0.6 ms at the realistic coefficients). With the second derelict loaded but dormant it costs 0; loaded and active it adds about a third. VS-A naive (1,200 nodes, 2,000 edges, 120 compartments) is 5.6 ms at the first-draft coefficients and about 28 ms at the realistic ones — the reason quiescence exists; at 20 % active it is about 1.1 ms per run at the first-draft figures. 820	**Diagnostics counters** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. 836	- **If two compartments are joined by an opening and the pressure gradient falls below `1 / (G_OPEN × A)` dkPa**: `Δn` floors to 0 and the rooms stop exchanging gas — **equalisation stalls within `⌈1/k⌉` mGU** of exact balance (10,000 mGU = 0.5 dkPa for a pinhole in a 20-tile room; 156 mGU for a door). This is expected behaviour, stated so QA does not file it: the residual is below the 10 dkPa key quantum and below any band boundary's hysteresis, and TD's truncation discipline (floor on non-negative magnitudes) buys exact conservation in exchange for it. Diagnostics: `graph_stall_edges` (count of open edges with `g ≠ 0` and `Δn` = 0 this run; informational; floors apply once, on the final division of D.1 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*).

No diagnostics — this is a dead room, which the MVP derelicts contain by design.

A hit in play is a content bug (a BURN footprint or a heater in a 4-tile closet), never a mechanic; every test suite asserts the counter is 0.

This is the MVP rule (`T_mach` has no inertia of its own; the machine's casing is a proxy, not a store); VS-A may add a persisted machine heat store if playtest wants a SCRAM to cost minutes. 920	- **If a structural invariant fails in `graph.propagate.failure` while a cascade is mid-flight** (phase 10 has queued `forced_mode_next` on twelve subjects and an edge endpoint is found pointing at a tombstone): the kernel's step-invariant path fires — FAULTED, `Dropped(FAULTED)` for the tick's commands, no P5 notification, no autosave; the partial writes of the run stay in the block for the diagnostic dump; the dev build halts, the release build returns to the menu. Mutators are written so that the only operations after the check are array appends, element writes and flag sets, with no lookup that can miss.
922	- **If the kernel pauses, snapshots or saves "mid-step"**: it cannot mid-hook — each hook is atomic inside P3 of its tick, every buffered delta is applied before its hook returns, and the kernel snapshots only at tick boundaries after P5. 1087	## Visual/Audio Requirements
1088	
1089	The Graph draws nothing and plays nothing. It owns the **semantics** that Failure & Trail, In-World Instruments and Adaptive Audio render, and it constrains them:
1090	
1091	- **Descriptors, not visuals.** Every presentation of a failure is derived from a `FailureDescriptor` (mode, medium, severity 0–4, intensity ‰, anchor ids, acoustic class, `alarm_eligible`). Medium selects the art bible's trail word — O₂ → mist, coolant → frost, power → scorch, fuel → drip, integrity → hairline/buckling — and severity selects the band; the Graph never names a colour, a sprite or a sound.
1092	- **One trail per source, continuous along its edge** (art bible rule). A descriptor carries the source anchor and the edge it travels, so a trail is thickest at the source and never appears at a node without upstream evidence on the connecting edge. Trails are on the consequence channel: the Perception Filter can neither remove nor add one, so an orphan trail cannot occur.
1093	- **Spatial gradients are presentation.** Atmosphere is per compartment; frost creeping from a leak point is Failure & Trail's interpolation of the true compartment value plus the leak anchor and its age — honest to the Graph, never a per-tile simulation.
1094	- **Lamps dim honestly.** `served_pm` drives lamp brightness under brownout; a lamp never renders brighter than the power it is served (P1).
1095	- **Audio is true-state.** Hiss pitch/rate, hum and ticking are read from true values and belong to the consequence channel: a hallucination may neither remove a real hiss nor add a sound in a witness acoustic class (the eight LS-14 ids; WIND is the whistle; there is no loop-whisper class) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from adaptive-audio-and-tells)* (phantom-entity audio is the Filter's own, in its own classes); `alarm_eligible` (severity ≥ 3) is the only state in which an alarm-class sound or the Alarm Red sweep may play — never as the first warning.
1096	- **The first fault the player ever sees** is the seeded coolant frost trail running from the cryo bay leak to the far wall (art bible carried element).

1100	## Game Feel
1101	
1102	The Graph's feel is **slow burn, then cascade, then silence** — and the player should be able to say afterwards exactly why.
1103	
1104	- **A body that decays on its own clock.** Left alone, the home-ship wears: its authored faults run on minute-scale clocks (first tell to lethal ≈ 6 min for an O₂ pinhole in a room, ≈ 9 for the ship; 4.5 for a power overload branch; 9 for coolant; 12 for hull fatigue), and the machines that keep it alive wear a little every hour they run (`W_DUTY`), so a fully repaired ship is quiet, never safe. Nothing resolves itself.
1105	- **Long tell, short collapse.** A long tell, a spreading wrongness, a short collapse, then silence. The real tells run in minutes (D.15); the sim's own floor beneath them is `W_MIN_WARNING_S` = 10 s of two-channel physical warning before any loss the ship causes by itself, so "death is a bitch" is always nameable, never arbitrary. Horrors and the web have their own tells (Attention, Horror Entities) that must precede anything they do to the ship.
1106	- **Every fix moves a cost.** Power for air (the scrubber draws, the web watches); air for heat; a sealed door for a stranded room; a weld for a leaky seam; a salvaged battery for a dark ship. Triage of five coupled loops, not a repair list.
1107	- **Derelicts are already dead.** They don't tick until the player brings power; then faults that wake wear twice as fast (the wear clock, not the leaks and not the drains) — but still warn first *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; a breach is already past its tell by the time the hull gives.
1108	- **Rooms never quite settle.** A faint draught at a nearly-shut hatch is real and stays; two rooms do not balance to the last breath. Expected, not a bug.
1109	- **Silence is a tell, and there are two silences** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. A leak that has stopped hissing has either nothing left to leak (its descriptor is gone) or a closed valve upstream (the mode stays, `intensity_pm` is 0 and `isolated_at_step` is set). The sound cannot tell them apart; the valve lever can — its position is a TRUTH world-state witness (LS-14) — and so does the trail, which stops growing but stays. Silence alone never means "fixed".
1110	- **The dark has a clock** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. The same issue applies to pa_frozen: a forced FREEZE failure with zero flow capacity is a dead frozen pipe, yet it still qualifies for alarm mode 4 and would sound on first boarding of Derelict A. This seems like a real consequence of the binding ruling that I should flag as inconsistent with the "never fires for dead faults" guarantee.

And since the player boards A right at the start, that alarm would sound permanently from step one — which does feel like a Pillar 2 violation ("dread before chaos"). I'd lean toward rating it RECOMMENDED rather than BLOCKING, since this is a design-intent conflict rather than something literally broken or impossible to implement.

I'll flag it as RECOMMENDED: add a liveness clause so the alarm only sounds under genuine fault conditions, or have CD explicitly sign off that the sustained annunciator on Derelict A is intentional, and also note DA's stale unresolved flag. findings.section: LS-11 SHORT predicate (L135) / LS-14 mode table row 2 (L184) vs D.9 short burn (L577) / PWR-OVL (L141, L771, L1200, L1293)
findings.finding: CARRIED OVER, third pass. SHORT is defined as 'hp < HP_FAIL under load', and D.9's burn guard requires the cable to be 'still in mode SHORT (LS-11)'. At the PWR-OVL registry defaults the cable reaches hp = 10000 - 4*1750 = 3000 exactly on step 1750. An implementer who follows the mode table and one who follows the D.9 prose build different games, and the D.9 prose is not what the table says.
findings.fix: Define SHORT's LIVE predicate for CABLE as 'FAILED (hp <= HP_FAIL) and a live source (S + D > 0) in an island at either end, until repair or breaker open', and for CABLE_JUNCTION / LOAD as 'hp <= HP_FAIL and served_pm > 0'. Change the wording in LS-11 (L135), the mode-table row (L184) and the D.9 guard (L577) together. Read literally, the short burn never starts, so DESTROYED at step 2500 (C1, the R21 power band 3.8-5.2 min, the AC at L1200 and L1293) is unreachable. An implementer who follows the mode table and one who follows the D.9 prose build different games, and the D.9 prose is not what the table says.
findings.fix: Define SHORT's LIVE predicate for CABLE as 'FAILED (hp <= HP_FAIL) and a live source (S + D > 0) in an island at either end, until repair or breaker open', and for CABLE_JUNCTION / LOAD as 'hp <= HP_FAIL and served_pm > 0'. Change the wording in LS-11 (L135), the mode-table row (L184) and the D.9 guard (L577) together. Add one Section H assertion that the PWR-OVL cable has hp 2996 on step 1751 and reads mode SHORT on step 1750 or 1751 (state which).

findings.section: LS-14 AIRFLOW intensity_pm (L166, L197) vs descriptor provenance (L208), LS-22 (L264) and AC L1271 / L1298
findings.finding: CARRIED OVER, third pass. AIRFLOW intensity_pm = abs(dP)/1000 with dP in dkPa. A legal interior gradient is under 1000 dkPa (the example 850 dkPa weld hatch gives 0; even a full-vacuum 1000 gives 1), so the value is 0 for essentially every real draught. L208 puts AIRFLOW in the flow-fraction list and says a flow-fraction descriptor at intensity_pm 0 is silent (closed-valve rule), and L1272 repeats it. The doc's primary pressure witness (LS-22 row 'AIRFLOW draught and dust at openings') is therefore silent by its own rule, and the MVP must-prove 'draught between the rooms when the hatch opens' (L1298) cannot be met. SEAL_STRAIN in the same table already uses min(1000, abs(dP)).
findings.fix: Set AIRFLOW intensity_pm = max(1, min(1000, abs(dP))) in the field table (L166), the mode table (L197) and the SEAL_STRAIN/AIRFLOW example in D.14. Update the Section H witness criterion (L1271) to assert intensity_pm > 0 for an 850 dkPa gradient and the AA/F&T silence-threshold note in OQ 33.

findings.section: LS-13 (a) consequences: SEVERED (8) and dead authored hazard modes
findings.finding: New with the alarm ruling and unstated. SEVERED is alarm-capable and, as a forced mode, takes sev >= 3 (L133, L425). Every player salvage (M6) leaves an open_end SEVERED edge, and a RAGGED cut leaves SEVERED stubs plus an A_CUT BREACH sev 4. An exogenous event still sets warn_since_step (L863), so 100 steps later alarm_eligible is true and alarm_sections() holds the body the player stands on; the ship klaxon, suit.alarm and the HUD sixth mark fire about 10 s after the player's own verb and stay on until cap_port. This applies to a power stub that leaks nothing (TICK only). The same keyed-on-mode rule means Derelict A's dead forced-FREEZE pipe pa_frozen (sev 4) and its dried LEAK pb_leak (intensity_pm 0, sev 3) become alarm_eligible 100 steps after the first boarding (DA L336 states this and 'takes no position'). That is the 'alarm for a dead, silent fault' the blocker's rationale called a Pillar 2 breach. No Boarding, HUD or Audio text covers either case.
findings.fix: Decide and write it in LS-13 (a): either (i) add a liveness clause (alarm_capable additionally requires intensity_pm > 0, or for no-intensity modes served/cap > 0, so a dried LEAK, a cap-0 frozen pipe and a no-flow power stub never alarm), or (ii) state explicitly that SEVERED and dead hazard-mode faults do alarm and get the creative-director to confirm that Derelict A rings from first boarding. Add one Section H criterion for the chosen behaviour (salvage a scrubber on Derelict A; assert alarm_sections() before and after cap_port). Then remove the stale [UNV] in DA L336.

findings.section: LS-17 / M19 / Edge Cases 'section is dormant' (L222, L246, L926) / AC L1258
findings.finding: CARRIED OVER. The compartment warn trackers warn_since_o2/p/t (LS-13 (b), persisted absolute step stamps) are not in M19's advance list. A dormant section's bands are frozen, so on resume warn_elapsed_x = step_no - warn_since_x includes the whole dormant time and gate_open is true at once. That counts as served a warning the player never witnessed, the exact defect LS-17 fixed for nodes and edges. AC L1258 checks only node, edge and seam stamps.
findings.fix: Add the three trackers (while their warn_bits bit is set) to the M19 resume advance in LS-17, the M19 table row and Edge Cases L926, and extend AC L1258 with a THIN compartment dormant for 3000 steps whose alarm_eligible stays false until 100 further steps run.

findings.section: LS-8 topology refresh (L112, L117) vs LS-19 eager ensure_derived (L250) vs L893
findings.finding: New from this pass's edit. LS-8 now says the topology refresh (components, power trees, path_cap, degrees, deg_max) runs at the head of the first Graph hook after a structural mutator and costs nothing while topo_dirty is clear. LS-19 and Edge Cases L893 say ensure_derived() is eager: every structural mutator and post_restore rebuilds the derived caches (LS-21 lists components, trees, path_cap, degrees among them) in the mutator, so reads never rebuild. Both cannot own the same rebuild. The consequences differ: loop_component() / can_join after a weld return stale or fresh data, and the AC budgets (weld_join <= 0.2 ms, L1223, L1285) either include or exclude the rebuild.
findings.fix: Split the cache list. State that ensure_derived() eagerly rebuilds only the read-side caches (id maps, neighbors, nodes_in, hull_segments_of, V / exposed_tiles) and that components, trees, path_cap, degrees stay topo_dirty work done at hook head (loop_component then reads the last hook's value and says so), or drop the hook-head wording. Align the two AC time budgets.

findings.section: Edge Cases 'weld joins a dead section' (L884) vs D.6 / D.9
findings.finding: CARRIED OVER. The edge case says a dead short (FAILED CABLE_JUNCTION at hp 2000 under load) makes the home-ship seam cable overload per D.9 with an OVERLOAD descriptor from the first step. No formula draws extra current for SHORT. A FAILED junction has cap 0, splits the island, and carries no load, so rho on the seam cable is its ordinary served-power rho. The scorch the text promises cannot be derived.
findings.fix: Rewrite the entry to what the formulas do: closing the breaker onto a dead branch merges islands; a FAILED junction has cap 0, so the derelict side stays unserved (STARVE) and the seam cable carries the served power only. If a short-circuit overload is wanted, add a D.6 term (a SHORT node draws N x req_w from its island) and its cap/rho arithmetic; do not leave a consequence with no formula.

findings.section: D.14 q / Q_MIN (L733) and build assertion (L1083) vs registry weld_quality (entities.yaml L5124) and Assembly D.1 (L536)
findings.finding: CARRIED OVER owner conflict. The registry owner (Modular Ship Assembly) and its GDD define Q_MIN = max(400, ceil(LEAK_HP / 10)). The Graph defines Q_MIN = max(400, ceil(max(LEAK_HP, BREACH_HP) / 10)) and asserts 10 x Q_MIN >= max(LEAK_HP, BREACH_HP). They agree at the defaults (both 400) and diverge as soon as BREACH_HP is tuned above LEAK_HP. G1 says the owner wins and the Graph conforms or the owner is changed; the Graph only 'routes' it and Assembly was not updated in this pass.
findings.fix: Preferred (G6, owner adds the missing surface): edit Assembly D.1 and the registry expression to max(LEAK_HP, BREACH_HP), keep the Graph text. Otherwise conform the Graph. Either way the Graph build assertion and the registry must say the same thing.

findings.section: Tuning Knobs 'Registered / Not yet registered' paragraph (L1085) and OQ 41
findings.finding: CARRIED OVER, stale after this pass. The paragraph still says SHORT_BURN_BP_PER_STEP, THAW_ROLL_STEPS, BURST_HP_TO and BURST_P_PM are not registered, BATT_DIS_CAP is 'registered at 2000, now 1000', and GRAPH_HOOK_BUDGET_MS reads 'per run'. The registry now has all four (one entry each), BATT_DIS_CAP value 1000, and GRAPH_HOOK_BUDGET_MS 'per hook tick'. OQ 41 still lists BATT_DIS_CAP, GRAPH_HOOK_BUDGET_MS and weld_quality as registry requests.
findings.fix: Move those names into the 'Registered' list, delete the 'Not yet registered' sentence except weld_quality (see the Q_MIN finding), and strike the matching registry items from OQ 41.

findings.section: Stale stagger text: LS-26 (L281), D.16 Example (L814), header change log (L12)
findings.finding: CARRIED OVER. LS-26 'Waits for VS-A' still lists 'the hook stagger', although LS-8, D.16 rung 1, the AC at L1153 and OQ 31 make it the MVP baseline. The D.16 example says 'the stagger would put about 0.3 ms on each of three ticks' (conditional, but it is already in force). L12 still says the stagger was 'Declined or deferred' (it carries a Reversed marker, which is acceptable).
findings.fix: Delete 'the hook stagger' from LS-26's VS-A list (keep quiescence and compaction), and change L814 to 'the stagger (baseline) puts about 0.3 ms on each of three ticks'. Re-grep the 21 'stagger' hits for other conditional wording.

findings.section: D.16 / LS-24 / GRAPH_HOOK_BUDGET_MS / AC S1 (L813, L277, L1028, L1284)
findings.finding: CARRIED OVER. D.16's own realistic estimate puts the largest single staggered hook at about 0.6 ms, above the 0.5 ms P99 it asks for, and it says MVP has no rung after rung 1, so S1 is predicted to fail on the document's own numbers. The single 0.5 / 1.0 ms figure is also not scaled for RM-DECK (33.3 ms ceiling at 30 fps, a slower CPU), and LS-24 says 'pass needs P99 within the R12 headroom of the frame ceiling', which mixes a hook-share bound with a frame-ceiling headroom rule. The criterion is spike-gated and PLACEHOLDER, so this is not a blocker, but it is a known red.
findings.fix: State the share per machine (RM-DESKTOP 0.5 / 1.0 ms; RM-DECK a separate PLACEHOLDER, for example 1.0 / 2.0 ms), say which of the two R12 rules is the pass line (share bound AND frame P99 <= 90 % of the ceiling), and replace 'no rung after rung 1' with the action if S1 misses (re-request the share, Open Question 31, naming the owner).

findings.section: Acceptance Criteria, D1 bot (L1296) and Edge Cases D1 (L897)
findings.finding: CARRIED OVER. The criterion passes whatever the bot does: 'by step 18,000 the ship's own clocks have produced a live descriptor of sev >= 3' is true because of the authored faults (4.5-12 min), so it does not test the sealed-room strategy it names.
findings.fix: Rewrite: 'GIVEN F-MVP with every authored fault removed except hull-fatigued outer plates, and the D1 bot (all doors closed, one crew in the scrubber room, no commands), WHEN 70,000 runs execute (soak), THEN the reactor SCRAMs by fuel starve between runs 66,600 and 67,500 (20,000 mL at 0.3 mL/step), the bot's room reaches band_o2 THIN within 2,000 runs of the scrubber losing power, and no run before 60,000 has a sev >= 3 descriptor in the bot's room.' This tests the physics, not the content.

findings.section: D.15 HEALTHY 'For alarms' (L778) vs AC L1189
findings.finding: CARRIED OVER, plus a new gap. The text implies a fresh 100-step gate on entering FREEZING, but the t tracker opened at COOL (sev 1), so the gate is already open and the annunciator sounds as soon as band_t reaches FREEZING. L778 also says the clause has 'an (auto) criterion in Section H', but the closed-door AC (L1189) has no alarm assertion. Arithmetic: an isolated V 30 room with S_ext 22 has plate tau 16,364 steps; from 20 C to -15 C is ln(50/15) = 1.2 tau, about 19,700 steps, so FREEZING is not reached inside the AC's 18,000 runs. The clause is untested.
findings.fix: Reword: 'the annunciator sounds when band_t first reads FREEZING, because the t tracker has been open since COOL'. Add to L1189 (or a slow sibling): in the closed-door ship run 24,000 runs; assert alarm_eligible is false on every run before the first FREEZING run and true from that run for ATMO_COLD, and alarm_sections() holds the section from then.

findings.section: D.15 DOOR-BREACH fixture (L781) vs AC L1204 and Suit anchor moment
findings.finding: New ambiguity. The fixture is 'V 20, A 64 to vacuum'. If it is a stored OPENING to EXTERIOR, the descriptor is AIRFLOW (never capable) and 'alarm_sections() is empty to step 124' holds. If it is a DESTROYED hull segment (a virtual A_hole 64), a BREACH sev 4 descriptor exists from its first run and, with its gate opening at step 100, alarm_sections() is non-empty from step 100, contradicting the AC. Suit describes it only as 'a door-sized opening on a V 20 room'.
findings.fix: Pin the fixture definition in D.15 and Section H (state which, and which descriptors exist from step 1), and recompute L1204's alarm_sections() boundary from that definition.

findings.section: D.5 Example (L470) and D.1 Output Range (L363)
findings.finding: CARRIED OVER arithmetic slips. L470: 'net +300 mGU/step, climbs toward 210 at 0.015 dkPa/step - about 7 min from THIN back to NORMAL'. THIN to NORMAL (p_o2 145 to 185) is 40 dkPa = 800,000 mGU / 300 = 2,667 steps = 4.4 min; 7.2 min is to the 210 setpoint (4,333 steps). Survival-clock figures propagate to other GDDs. D.1 says 'a 20-tile room empties through an open hatch in about 160 steps' - that is the e-folding time 1/k = 156, not emptying.
findings.fix: State '4.4 min to NORMAL, 7.2 min to the setpoint' in D.5, and 'falls to 1/e of its gas in about 156 steps; LOW in 56 steps' in D.1.

findings.section: LS-1 (e) heat invariant / LS-16 discard_section / M4 (L72, L220)
findings.finding: CARRIED OVER, latent until M4 is promoted (VS-A). The gas, coolant and fuel invariants carry discarded_* terms; the heat invariant has no discarded-heat term, so a jettisoned section (compartment U and reservoir heat store leave the world) breaks exact heat conservation. The property test covers weld and cut only.
findings.fix: Add a discarded_heat_mdj counter credited by discard_section (compartment U plus RESERVOIR heat stores), include it in the heat sum, and add it to the S2 property test; or mark the heat invariant 'MVP: no discard' with a VS-A note.

findings.section: Untestable ACs: L1294, L1272, L1307, L1299
findings.finding: L1294: 'GIVEN Suit & Equipment's survival-clock fixtures, WHEN run headless through the Graph harness, THEN each reaches its stated time +/-15 %' names no fixture and no time. L1272 and L1306-L1307 still say 'when written' / 'MVP playtest reports ...' for sources that are all written. L1307 'tense and absorbing for 30+ minutes' is a hypothesis, correctly listed under 'Gaps / untestable', but it sits in the AC set.
findings.fix: L1294 -> 'GIVEN the DOOR-BREACH, O2-ROOM and pod-leg fixtures of suit-and-equipment.md D.1 / D.3, WHEN run through the Graph harness, THEN Suit's printed times (list them: LOW 5.6 s, DECOMP 14 s, VACUUM 36 s, ANOXIC 6.1 min for N_crew 1) are reproduced within +/-15 % (+/-2 % for the single-mechanism rows).' L1272 -> name the four files (failure-and-trail-system.md, in-world-instruments-and-inspect-view.md, adaptive-audio-and-tells.md, perception-filter.md) and the greps. L1307 -> move to Open Question 12 as a playtest question, or rewrite: 'GIVEN >= 3 outside playtest sessions, THEN report the share reaching the weld before first death; <2 of 3 reopens Section G tuning.'

findings.section: Dependencies / Bidirectional consistency (L982) and OQ 33; systems-index.md
findings.finding: The systems index still has no Life-Support Graph edge for Interaction (row 8), Derelict Authoring (14), Boarding & Salvage (15), Web Map & Transit (16), Sanity (19), Perception Filter (20), HUD (21) or Debug Overlay (26). The design rules require dependencies to be bidirectional. L982 and OQ 33 record this as a routed note, but G6 now allows the edit.

findings.section: LS-14 field table row alarm_eligible (L171) and mode 25 warn_elapsed
findings.finding: New stale cross-reference from this pass: the alarm_eligible row says 'constant false for modes 24-27', but LS-13 (a) / D.11 make 6 STARVE and 10 WORN constant false too. The warn_elapsed row covers OPENING 24 / 26 but not 25 PUDDLE or 27 PATCH_WEEP.
findings.fix: Change to 'constant false for modes 6, 10 and 24-27' and state warn_elapsed for 25 / 27 (the PUDDLE tracker, or 0).

findings.section: Rationale tags: local R1-R24 vs delegated R1-R21
findings.finding: The Cross-References glossary defines R1-R24 as the 2026-10-26 orchestrator rulings, but the delegated rulings of 2026-10-27/28 reuse R12 (reference machines vs local 'islands are trees'), R13 (vs local 'dormant resumes'), R14 and R21 (vs local 'time-band targets'). Section H tags such as [D.15; R21; LS-26] (L1293, L1295) and [D.6; R12; OQ 24] (L1185) mean the local ids, while the same file also says 'delegated ruling R12/R21'. A reader or QA lead cannot tell which is meant.

findings.finding: attention-system.md cites Graph line anchors that moved (LSG:281 for 'the Graph reads nothing from Attention', LSG:104, LSG:199); derelict-authoring-handmade-kits.md L336 still carries '[UNV: Graph, the LS-13 (a) wording of capability for mode 6 ...]' although L135 / L152 now state it. Neither breaks a rule.
findings.fix: Replace the line anchors with rule ids (LS-26, LS-8, LS-19) and strike the DA [UNV].

data.summary:
Fifth pass, read-only. Verdict: NEEDS REVISION, now two small blockers away from approval. The one prior blocker (LS-13 (a) alarm_capable versus WORN) is fully resolved in the GDD, the registry, the new Section H criterion (L1208) and the siblings (Suit, HUD and Audio cite the registry; Derelict Authoring has the note). All 8 sections are present, all dependency GDDs exist (4 VS systems are undesigned, non-blocking per R9), no R20/R21 markers are left open, and R12-R14 are applied consistently. Sibling hook offsets (Suit 2, Attention 0, Emitter 4, Sanity tolerates_stale) match LS-8.

Two blockers remain, both carried over from the previous passes and both checked against the arithmetic at registry defaults. (1) SHORT is defined as 'hp < HP_FAIL under load', but the PWR-OVL cable is FAILED at exactly hp 3000 with cap 0, so the D.9 short burn never starts and DESTROYED at step 2500 (C1, the R21 power band, the AC at L1200) is unreachable as written. (2) AIRFLOW intensity_pm = abs(dP)/1000 is 0 for any interior gradient, and the doc says a flow-fraction descriptor at 0 is silent, so the draught, the primary pressure witness (LS-22) and the MVP must-prove 'draught when the hatch opens', is silent by the GDD's own rule. Each is a one-line fix.

Most of the earlier recommended list is still open (13 items carried over: the dormant compartment trackers, the weld-onto-dead-section short-current text, the Q_MIN owner conflict with Assembly, the stale registered/unregistered paragraph, the stagger left under 'Waits for VS-A', the D1 bot and S1 0.5 ms criteria, the D.15 HEALTHY alarm wording, and the D.5 / D.1 arithmetic slips). New from this pass: the alarm ruling's unstated consequences (SEVERED stubs and Derelict A's dead frozen pipe and dried leak would sound the klaxon 10 s after boarding or salvage), the overlap between LS-8's hook-head topology refresh and LS-19's eager ensure_derived, an ambiguous DOOR-BREACH fixture against the alarm_sections() AC, the systems-index edge gap, and a stale L171 field row. Rule-id collisions between the local R-tags and the delegated rulings are a NICE item.
